Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-892F80BC2E-98290
Requested service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Date of notice: 2026-08-21
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-17

To the Cigna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-21 (reference POC-892F80BC2E-98290). The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that Cigna reverse this determination based on the clinical documentation summarized below and enclosed with this letter.

Identification of the applicable policy

I understand this determination was reviewed under Cigna's medical coverage policy for this procedure, CMM-313: Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty, a Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management guideline developed by EviCore and applied by Cigna. I am proceeding on the understanding that the version of CMM-313 in effect on the date of this denial (August 21, 2026) is Version 1.0.2026, effective August 4, 2026. If Cigna instead applied a different policy, a different version, or additional internal criteria to my case, I ask that Cigna identify that document by name, number, and effective date, and provide me with a complete copy of the specific criteria applied, as I am entitled to receive under applicable claims-procedure regulations.

I want to be transparent about the limits of what I am able to quote directly from CMM-313 in this letter. I was able to obtain and directly quote the policy's "Definitions" and "General Guidelines" sections and its Tönnis Classification System (quoted below). I was not able to obtain a verbatim copy of the specific numbered indications in the "Hip Replacement" section (page 13 of the document, per its table of contents) that presumably lists the exact medical-necessity criteria for total hip replacement itself. Where I refer below to what those criteria are likely to require, I am doing so in my own words, based on the general structure and stated purpose of the guideline and on standard orthopedic practice — not by quoting Cigna's specific total-hip-replacement indications, which I have not seen in full. I ask that Cigna's reviewer apply the actual, complete criteria in the "Hip Replacement" section of CMM-313 V1.0.2026 to the facts below, and that a copy of that section be provided to me together with the outcome of this appeal.

From the portions of CMM-313 (V1.0.2026) I have reviewed directly, the policy states:

"The determination of medical necessity for the performance of hip resurfacing and hip replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis."

"For individuals with significant medical conditions or comorbidities, the risk/benefit of hip arthroplasty procedures should be clearly documented in the medical record."

The policy's Tönnis Classification System, used to grade osteoarthritis severity on plain radiographs, defines:

"Grade 1: sclerosis of the joint with slight joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation, and no or slight loss of femoral head sphericity"

"Grade 2: small cysts in the femoral head or acetabulum with moderate joint space narrowing and moderate loss of femoral head sphericity"

"Grade 3: large cysts in the femoral head or acetabulum, severe joint space narrowing or obliteration of the joint space, and severe deformity and loss of femoral head sphericity"

Application of the clinical record to the case-by-case medical necessity standard

The enclosed records document the following, which I ask be weighed under the "case-by-case" medical necessity standard quoted above and under the specific "Hip Replacement" criteria that Cigna's reviewer has access to in full:

1. Duration and severity of symptoms: I have had twelve months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest — well beyond any minimum symptom-duration threshold that would reasonably be applied to a total hip replacement request.

2. Documented, unsuccessful conservative (non-surgical) treatment:
- Ten weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait training, 24 visits completed between 2026-04-22 and 2026-07-01, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- Six months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13 that produced only three weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.
This history demonstrates a sustained, provider-directed course of non-surgical management, including medication, injection, and structured physical therapy, that has failed to control my symptoms.

3. Objective imaging findings: A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph on 2026-06-29 showed joint space narrowing to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. These findings — sclerosis, joint space narrowing, and osteophyte formation — are the defining radiographic features of osteoarthritis under the policy's own Tönnis Classification System, quoted above, and the degree of narrowing (1 mm, compared with a normal joint space of approximately 3–4 mm) reflects advanced, not mild, disease.

4. Functional impairment: I currently ambulate with a cane and am limited to walking approximately one city block. I am unable to put on my own shoes without assistance. On examination, I have a positive provocative test on the affected hip and pain-limited range of motion. These findings document substantial loss of hip function affecting my activities of daily living.

5. Absence of contraindications: I have no active local or systemic infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker. There is nothing in my history that should be treated as a risk factor weighing against surgery, consistent with the policy's own instruction (quoted above) that comorbidity-related risk/benefit concerns be "clearly documented in the medical record" — here, there are none to document.

6. Surgeon assessment: My treating orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has reviewed this history and recommends total hip replacement based on the failure of conservative management and the degree of functional limitation. [Please see the enclosed letter of medical necessity/operative plan from Dr. Okafor, NPI [insert NPI], for the surgeon's full clinical rationale.]

Taken together, I believe this record — twelve months of unrelieved pain, a fully documented and unsuccessful course of physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injection therapy, objective radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis under the plan's own Tönnis grading system, and significant functional loss (cane-dependent, one-block walking limit, unable to don shoes) — satisfies a medical-necessity standard for total hip replacement under any reasonable reading of CMM-313's "Hip Replacement" criteria. I ask that Cigna's appeal reviewer apply the full, specific criteria in that section to these facts and explain, in the event of a continued denial, exactly which specific criterion or criteria the record fails to meet, and provide a full copy of the criteria applied, so that any missing documentation can be supplied.

Requested outcome

I ask that Cigna:
1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for total hip replacement (CPT 27130); or
2. If the denial is upheld, provide me with the complete, verbatim medical-necessity criteria from the "Hip Replacement" section of CMM-313 (identifying the exact version and effective date applied to my claim) that were not met, so that my surgeon and I can respond with any additional documentation; and
3. Confirm my right to a second-level internal appeal and, if applicable, my right under Louisiana law to request an independent external review through the Louisiana Department of Insurance if the internal appeal process is exhausted.

Enclosed with this letter:
- Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-04-22 to 2026-07-01, 24 visits)
- Medication and injection history, including corticosteroid injection record dated 2026-05-13
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and radiology report dated 2026-06-29
- Clinic notes documenting functional status (cane use, one-block walking limitation, inability to don shoes unassisted) and physical examination findings (provocative testing, range of motion)
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, orthopedic surgery [enclose if available]
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-21

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the expected timeframe for a decision. I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address] if additional information is needed.

Sincerely,
